chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Ismail from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym said:

I witnessed Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) while he was being carried around the Kaaba in a litter, and he was severely ill. So whenever he reached the Yemeni Corner, he would order them, and they would place him on the ground. Then he would extend his hand from the opening of the litter until he dragged it on the ground, then he would say: 'Raise me.'
So when he did that repeatedly in each circuit, I said to him: 'May I be sacrificed for you, O son of the Messenger of Allah! Indeed, this is difficult for you.'
So he said: 'I heard Allah, Mighty and Majestic, saying: 'That they may witness benefits for them'.'
So I said: 'Benefits of the world or benefits of the Hereafter?' So he said: 'All.'

key_terms.الرُّكْنُ الْيَمَانِيُّ: The Yemeni Corner of the Kaaba
key_terms.مَحْمِلٌ: Litter or carriage for carrying a person

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and spiritual significance of a sick person performing Tawaf while being carried?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) physical devotion during his final illness, emphasizing the tactile connection with the Kaaba as a means of spiritual and worldly benefit. By citing the verse 'That they may witness benefits for them' (22:28), he clarifies that the ritual encompasses both material and spiritual gains, a point of scholarly discussion regarding the holistic nature of Hajj rituals. The act of dragging his hand on the ground at the Yemeni Corner underscores the importance of humility and physical engagement even in weakness.
